festivals.what: Saidaiji Eyo (Saidaiji Kannon-in, Okayama City): the third Saturday of February each year; about 10,000 men in loincloths contest two sacred sticks (shingi) thrown from the temple at 10 pm.

laws.rule: Okayama City bans smoking on roads, parks and other public places inside its street-smoking restricted zones (路上喫煙制限区域), shown on the city's zone maps. Smoking is allowed only at two smoking spots near Okayama Station. The city's page lists no fine for these zones; the ordinance keeps fines for a stricter special zone type.

laws.rule: Kurashiki City limits smoking around JR Kurashiki Station: smoking on public roads, in parks and other public places in the zone is allowed only at city-designated smoking areas. A city officer can order you to stop, and if you ignore the order a fine of up to JPY 10,000 (about A$90.23, RBA rate of 30 October 2026) can apply. Elsewhere in the city you are asked to avoid smoking while walking or cycling.
Kurashiki City has not announced an accommodation tax. Its study committee handed its report to the mayor on 4 June 2026; the page read gives no rate or start date, so check the city's announcements.

Okayama Youth Healthy Development Ordinance (岡山県青少年健全育成条例), art. 22. The ordinance sets the late-night period as 11 pm to 5 am. A guardian must try not to let a young person (generally under 18) go out in that period without special reason; the guardian's own duty has no penalty. Anyone else is barred from taking such a young person out, going about with them or keeping them out in that period without the guardian's consent or another proper reason. The offence for others carries a fine of up to JPY 300,000 (about A$2,707). Rates: RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = JPY 110.82.
